import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Least $k$ such that cyclotomic polynomial $\Phi_k(n)$ is prime

$a(n) = \min \{k \in \mathbb{N} \mid 0 < k \wedge \text{Prime}(|\Phi_k(n)|) \}$,
where $\Phi_k(n)$ is the $k$-th cyclotomic polynomial evaluated at $n$.

*References:*
- [A117545](https://oeis.org/A117545)-/

namespace OeisA117545

/-- Least $k > 0$ such that $|\Phi_k(n)|$ is prime, or $0$ if no such $k$ exists. -/
noncomputable def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k : ℕ | 0 < k ∧ ((Polynomial.cyclotomic k ℤ).eval (n : ℤ)).natAbs.Prime}

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 1. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 2 := by
  have h_least : IsLeast {k : ℕ | 0 < k ∧ ((Polynomial.cyclotomic k ℤ).eval (1 :
  ℤ)).natAbs.Prime} 2 := by
    constructor
    · simp only [Set.mem_ofPred_eq]
      refine ⟨by decide, ?_⟩
      have : Polynomial.cyclotomic 2 ℤ = Polynomial.X + 1 := Polynomial.cyclotomic_two ℤ
      rw [this]
      norm_num
    · intro k hk
      simp only [Set.mem_ofPred_eq] at hk
      by_contra! h
      have hk_pos := hk.1
      interval_cases k
      have hk2 := hk.2
      have h1 : Polynomial.cyclotomic 1 ℤ = Polynomial.X - 1 := Polynomial.cyclotomic_one ℤ
      rw [h1] at hk2
      revert hk2
      norm_num
  exact h_least.csInf_eq

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 2. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 2 := by
  have h_least : IsLeast {k : ℕ | 0 < k ∧ ((Polynomial.cyclotomic k ℤ).eval (2 :
  ℤ)).natAbs.Prime} 2 := by
    constructor
    · simp only [Set.mem_ofPred_eq]
      refine ⟨by decide, ?_⟩
      have : Polynomial.cyclotomic 2 ℤ = Polynomial.X + 1 := Polynomial.cyclotomic_two ℤ
      rw [this]
      norm_num
    · intro k hk
      simp only [Set.mem_ofPred_eq] at hk
      by_contra! h
      have hk_pos := hk.1
      interval_cases k
      have hk2 := hk.2
      have h1 : Polynomial.cyclotomic 1 ℤ = Polynomial.X - 1 := Polynomial.cyclotomic_one ℤ
      rw [h1] at hk2
      revert hk2
      norm_num
  exact h_least.csInf_eq

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 3. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 1 := by
  have h_least : IsLeast {k : ℕ | 0 < k ∧ ((Polynomial.cyclotomic k ℤ).eval (3 :
  ℤ)).natAbs.Prime} 1 := by
    constructor
    · simp only [Set.mem_ofPred_eq]
      refine ⟨by decide, ?_⟩
      have h1 : Polynomial.cyclotomic 1 ℤ = Polynomial.X - 1 := Polynomial.cyclotomic_one ℤ
      rw [h1]
      norm_num
    · intro k hk
      exact hk.1
  exact h_least.csInf_eq

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 4. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 1 := by
  have h_least : IsLeast {k : ℕ | 0 < k ∧ ((Polynomial.cyclotomic k ℤ).eval (4 :
  ℤ)).natAbs.Prime} 1 := by
    constructor
    · simp only [Set.mem_ofPred_eq]
      refine ⟨by decide, ?_⟩
      have h1 : Polynomial.cyclotomic 1 ℤ = Polynomial.X - 1 := Polynomial.cyclotomic_one ℤ
      rw [h1]
      norm_num
    · intro k hk
      exact hk.1
  exact h_least.csInf_eq

/--
Is $a(n)$ defined for all $n \ge 1$?
That is, for every $n \ge 1$, does there exist $k > 0$ such that $|\Phi_k(n)|$ is prime?-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    ∃ k > 0, ((Polynomial.cyclotomic k ℤ).eval (n : ℤ)).natAbs.Prime := by
  sorry

end OeisA117545

reformulations.difference: OEIS defines a potentially undefined least index with prime cyclotomic value. Lean tests the absolute value and returns 0 when there is no qualifying positive index.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For n ≥ 1, Mathlib proves Φ_k(n) ≥ 0, so taking natAbs does not change positive primality. The qualifying indices are strictly positive. Lean checks establish that a n = 0 exactly when no qualifying index exists, and, for k > 0, a n = k exactly when k is the least qualifying index. Thus the definition faithfully encodes the source's partial minimum using an unambiguous zero marker.

reformulations.difference: The source asks whether a(n) is defined for every n in its domain, whereas Lean explicitly asserts the existence of a prime-producing positive index for each positive n.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: OEIS has offset 1 and its program searches k starting at 1. A nonempty set of positive natural indices has a least element. In /workspace/review/equivalences.lean, I proved the displayed universal existence statement equivalent to ∀ n > 0, a n ≠ 0, and also proved its equivalence to the formulation using a positive prime equal to Φ_k(n), without an absolute value.

review.notes: Checked all six declarations. Direct OEIS entry pages were blocked, but the full entry was available through OEIS's own data export, dated 2026-09-07. It still asks “Is a(n) defined for all n?” and records no resolution, consistent with research open. The four value tests match the source and have no sorryAx dependencies. Additional Lean checks prove a(0)=0, absence of any witness at n=0, a(5)=3, a(9)=6, and the source's characterization a(n)=1 iff n−1 is prime for n>0. Executable small-index searches for n=1,…,10 match the b-file. Scratch files are in /workspace/review/; the reviewed file remains byte-for-byte identical to the committed file.
